title: DSSP: Diffusion State Space Policy with Hierarchical Full-History Conditioning
claim: Baselines without history lose track of task progress and stop early; conditioning on full history completes long-horizon sequences, with higher success rates.
layout: Left: two bar charts; right: two stacked filmstrip rows, left-to-right, ✗ vs ✓
description: The left column has two bar charts. The top chart shows RoboTwin (50 tasks) success rate for DP (34.5), SeedPolicy (42.8), DP3 (55.2) and Ours (62.3), with Ours in red. The bottom chart compares DP3 (yellow) and Ours (red) on three real-world tasks: Put Bottles, Object Swap and Morse Tapping, where Ours leads, e.g. 85 vs 15 on Morse Tapping. The right side has two filmstrip rows of six robot-arm photos joined by arrows. The top row, titled in red 'DP3 (History-Blind)', has the last three frames outlined in red. A dashed red arrow reads 'Lose progress and stop prematurely', with a red ✗ and 'Confuse tap count under visual aliasing'. The bottom row, titled in green 'The Proposed DSSP (Full History-Encoded)', has a solid green arrow reading 'Consistent progress toward task completion', with a green ✓. A banner at the bottom gives the task: 'Morse Tapping: Tap the target three times and return to the initial position.'
caption: The proposed \textbf{\ours{}} leverages full-history context to resolve visual aliasing when history-blind baselines lose track of task progress, enabling consistent execution in long-horizon tasks. \ours{} achieves superior success rates across both simulation tasks and real-world experiments.
abstract: Diffusion-based imitation learning has shown strong promise for robot manipulation. However, most existing policies condition only on the current observation or a short window of recent observations, limiting their ability to resolve history-dependent ambiguities in long-horizon tasks. To address this, we introduce \ours, a history-conditioned Diffusion State Space Policy that enables efficient, full-history conditioning for robot manipulation. Leveraging the continuous sequence modeling properties of State Space Models (SSMs), our history encoder effectively compresses the entire observation stream into a compact context representation. To ensure this context preserves critical information regarding future state evolution, the encoder is optimized with a dynamics-aware auxiliary training objective. This high-level context representation is then seamlessly fused with recent state observations to form a hierarchical conditioning mechanism for action generation. Furthermore, to maintain architectural consistency and minimize GPU memory overhead, we also instantiate the diffusion backbone itself using an SSM. Extensive experiments across simulation benchmarks and real-world manipulation tasks show that \ours achieves state-of-the-art performance with a significantly smaller model size, demonstrating superior efficiency of the hierarchical conditioning in capturing crucial information as the history length increases.
